content: We use a default train-validation-test split of 70-15-15 for each dataset, and use all 4 datasets (BF, BA, SFU and Sherlock). The results for BERT are taken from BIBREF12. The results for XLNet and RoBERTa are averaged across 5 runs for statistical significance. Figure FIGREF14 contains results for negation cue detection and scope resolution. We report state-of-the-art results on negation scope resolution on BF, BA and SFU datasets.
